source.title: Scaling Law of Neural Koopman Operators
source.authors: Abulikemu Abuduweili; Yu-Yang Pang; Fei-Han Li; Chang-Liu Liu

record.file_problem: The full paper text, including its appendix and references, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps data size and latent dimension for neural Koopman models in robotic dynamics and reports fitted prediction-error scaling, extending scaling-law analysis to a different model and training setting. It does not test language-model cross-entropy scaling.
record.gate_note: The study measures held-out prediction MSE for robotic dynamics models, not language-model pretraining cross-entropy. Its results bear on V5's claim about power-law behavior in other training settings and on V7's setup-dependent fitted exponents. The cited language-model scaling results are background only. Regularizer and control outcomes are not rows here because they do not test the scaling form.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws of held-out prediction MSE against training-set size and latent dimension for neural Koopman dynamics models in six robotic environments and a synthetic polynomial system. This is a new modality and training setting, so it bears on V5. It measures no language-model loss, so V1–V4 and V6 are untested. Its exponent differences across physical systems are not the setup or fitting choices that V7 names for published LM laws.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that sampling error decays with data size and projection error with latent dimension, so latent dimension should grow with data (m≳n ln n, with m≳40 n ln n as a heuristic). They add that their covariance and inverse-control regularizers leave open-loop prediction error nearly unchanged (<5%) but improve closed-loop control.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses fitted power laws of robotic Koopman prediction MSE against dataset size and latent dimension, rather than the original language-model held-out cross-entropy sweeps over parameters, tokens, and compute. It also studies a coupled data/dimension heuristic, not a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Exponent changes with environment and system complexity; sample-size and latent-dimension exponents differ; latent-dimension scaling depends on dataset size and the coupled-scaling data-sufficiency coefficient. Low-data G1 and Go2 settings show worsening error as latent dimension increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Fitted exponents differ strongly across physical systems: αn from 0.34 to 4.3, and αm falls as polynomial nonlinearity rises (2.64 to 1.64). The authors relate exponents to the system's spectral decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling exponents of learned dynamics models depend on the intrinsic smoothness and spectral complexity of the modelled system.

record.problems: Theoretical rates depend on stated assumptions including i.i.d. sampling, well-conditioned Gram matrices, spectral decay, and subspace approximation; the authors note that real locomotion includes non-stationary trajectories and hybrid contact dynamics. Empirical exponent estimates are reported without uncertainty intervals. Several latent-dimension polynomial fits have modest R² values (0.25 to 0.74).
record.rows_left_out: Auxiliary-regularizer ablations, condition-number analyses, and downstream MPC/control metrics were left out because they do not measure the scaling form itself. Other architecture comparisons and reported control outcomes are in Sections VI-B and VI-C and Tables III-V.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out cross-entropy versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to larger runs is attempted.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The m≳40 n ln n heuristic is a data-sufficiency rule, not a compute-optimal split.
No depth/width shape variation at fixed parameter count.

Image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer. Compute as a scaling axis. True parameter-count scaling (latent dimension only). Ranges beyond about two orders of magnitude (m from 1k to 140k; n from 2^2 to 2^9).
Downstream predictability. Control metrics are reported, but the authors note control scaling is 'nuanced' and they are not fit as scaling laws.
Effects of parameter counting, training schedule or fitting method on exponents. Disagreement among published laws.

missing.what: Per-latent-multiplier sample-size exponents (e.g. Franka 0.3–0.7, G1 0.6–0.8, Kinova 1.2–1.7)
Per-dataset-size latent-dimension exponents. These include near-zero G1 values at m≤16k and Go2 values of about 0.4–0.5.

record.verdict_notes: V7 links were dropped: the study's exponent variation reflects different physical systems, not the LM setup or fitting choices V7 names. The low-data reversal (r33, r34) is excluded from verdicts because data is the bottleneck there. Sweep ranges span about two orders of magnitude. No uncertainty is given on the exponents.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out cross-entropy versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their growth with compute.
Architecture-shape effects at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities such as image and video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer; no language-model loss or cross-entropy is measured.
Downstream-task predictability from language-model scale or pretraining loss.

The study shows exponent variation across its robotic environments and nonlinearity settings, but does not compare language-model published laws, test parameter-counting or training-schedule choices, or study a compute-optimal split.

relationships.condition: Sample-size sweeps in six robotic environments and the polynomial system
relationships.reason: Prediction MSE fits A·m^-α+C with αm 0.49–1.44 in robotic systems (r1–r6) and R²≥0.99 in the polynomial system (r13–r17).
relationships.display_finding: Prediction MSE fitted A·m^-α+C with robotic-system exponents of 0.49–1.44 and R²≥0.99 in the polynomial system.

relationships.condition: Latent-dimension (capacity) sweeps in robotic systems with high data or coupled data scaling
relationships.reason: Error decays as a power law in latent dimension when m≥10^4 (r7–r12) or when m scales with n ln n (r23–r32).
relationships.display_finding: Error decayed as a power law in latent dimension when m≥10^4 or when sample size scaled with n ln n.

relationships.condition: Synthetic polynomial system, latent-dimension sweep at m=140k
relationships.reason: Power-law fits are poor (R² 0.25–0.74) and exponents are near zero (0.02–0.28), so capacity scaling is weak there (r18–r22).
relationships.display_finding: Power-law fits achieved R²=0.25–0.74 with small exponents of 0.02–0.28, indicating weak capacity scaling.
